children: Wall Street climbed Monday as investors positioned for a U.S.-China trade de-escalation while watching developments surrounding U.S.-Iran negotiations.
said markets appeared to be pricing in geopolitical deals, including “an October surprise” involving the U.S. and Iran and progress from the Trump-Xi summit.
“The markets seem to be pricing” both developments, Tokic stated, noting that crude oil had fallen nearly 5% as expectations for easing tensions supported sentiment.
advanced +2.2%, with technology stocks leading the move.

However, Tokic said the bond market was signaling caution. Two-year Treasury yields edged higher, while the 10-year yield remained just below 5%, suggesting investors were not accepting the market’s geopolitical narrative.
“This is the market climbing the wall of worries,” Tokic said, pointing to a Shiller price-to-earnings ratio above 40.
He warned that failure to deliver the expected agreements could trigger a correction, with higher oil prices and Treasury yields providing signals for investors to monitor.

title: SA analyst: Stocks surge as oil slides, but the bond market signals caution
